sections.h2: What the Register of Deeds does for a home seller
sections.html:
The Iosco County Register of Deeds files and keeps every deed, mortgage, survey, land contract, condominium and subdivision document for real estate in the county. The county's own records begin in 1858. All of them have been digitized, and the online index reaches back to the early 1970s. Anything older is searched in person at the office, or by a title company you hire.

Tawas City is the seat. Selling a house here means the closing deed gets filed with this office. The office has no forms, is not staffed by attorneys, and will not advise on legal questions or prepare papers, so line up a lawyer or title company for that part.

A deed costs $30 to file. Some documents, such as a discharge of mortgage, an assignment of mortgage or an oil and gas paper, cross-reference other instruments, and each cross-reference after the first adds $3. Two payees are involved, so write two checks when a treasurer certification is needed.

sections.h2: Which documents need a tax certification?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts, and any other paper containing a Warrant and Defend or Covenant clause need a tax certification. The $5 payment goes to the Iosco County Treasurer, not to the Register of Deeds. Ask your closing agent to add it to the settlement statement.

Quitclaim deeds carry no covenant of warranty. Whether yours needs a certification is a question for the Register of Deeds before you submit it.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on an Iosco County sale
sections.html:
Michigan taxes deeds that convey property for money twice, once for the state and once for the county. The Resources page of the Iosco Register of Deeds carries three PDFs: a Transfer Tax Chart, a county exemption list and a state exemption list. Ask the office, or open that chart, for the exact dollar amount at your sale price.

Both statutes (MCL 207.505 for the county tax, MCL 207.526 for the state tax) shield some transfers entirely. Examples that come up in house deals:

  • An instrument with consideration under $100.
  • A deed used to confirm a title already held, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed that creates a joint tenancy when one of the people already owns the property.
  • A transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed or government-made loan under the county act, and any mortgage foreclosure under the state act.

If one fits your sale, the deed has to cite it on its face.

sections.h2: Michigan filing rules an Iosco County deed must meet
sections.html:
The state recording statutes, chiefly MCL 565.201 and 565.8, govern the format of every deed, and the Iosco office insists on an original with original signatures. Court orders and death certificates must carry a certified raised seal. Beyond that, county offices across Michigan flag these points:

  • Signatures are typed or printed beneath, and the notary acknowledgment matches those names.
  • The paper lists who drafted it, with name and address.
  • A deed to survivors comes with a certified death certificate on record.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded as its own document.
  • Anything in a language other than English has a written English translation attached.

A rejected deed pushes a closing back, so have the preparer check the document against the Iosco office's own requirements page before it goes in.

sections.h2: From closing to a filed deed
sections.html:
Most of the sequence happens before anyone walks into the Tawas City office, and a short checklist keeps the file complete:

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney or title company, since the office will not prepare it.
  • Sign it in front of a Michigan notary, using original signatures only.
  • Add the tax certification request if the deed has warranty language, with a separate $5 check to the County Treasurer.
  • Calculate the transfer tax from the county chart, or note the exemption on the deed.
  • Submit the deed with a $30 check to the Register of Deeds, adding $3 for each extra cross-reference where one applies.
  • Confirm the filing later through the DoxPop search to see that the document shows up in the index.

The search index reaches back only to the early 1970s, but a deed from this closing will be in it, so a quick lookup afterward confirms the record is complete.

Search recorded documents through the county's DoxPop link, or visit the office. Staff will not run genealogy searches on your behalf, though visitors may use the records themselves. A Property Watch service from DoxPop sends a notice when a new document is recorded against a property you name.

If you want a copy of your deed, you can get one online or at the counter for $1 a page. Paying off a mortgage does not produce a new deed, since your lender records a discharge and your original deed remains the proof of title.

Delinquent tax on the parcel is something to settle before the deed is filed. Ask the Iosco County Treasurer for the amount owed and give it to your closing agent, who can pay it from the sale proceeds. The tax certification for a warranty deed is the Treasurer's confirmation that the taxes are in order, so an open balance can hold up the paperwork. Sellers who want to avoid lender delays sometimes choose a cash sale, which still ends with the same deed, certification and filing.

Iosco is a Lake Huron county where most residents live along the US-23 shoreline in East Tawas, Tawas City and Oscoda. The population estimate for July 2025 is 25,266. There are 20,221 housing units but only 11,713 households, and 41.3 percent of the units were vacant in the 2020 census, a sign of the cottages and seasonal houses common here. Owners hold 82.1 percent of the occupied homes. A typical owned home is valued at $142,200, and median rent is $719 a month.

A change of ownership lifts the cap on taxable value the following calendar year, as Michigan Treasury explains in its guidance on Proposal A. The affected buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the local assessor. Which exemptions avoid uncapping is spelled out in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act.

Iosco County has an Equalization department and a Treasurer's Office. Ask them how a specific parcel is assessed and billed.

faqs.q: What does the Iosco office charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: $30, with $3 more for each additional cross-referenced instrument on documents such as mortgage discharges. Copies are $1 a page and certified copies are $5 plus $1 a page.

faqs.q: Do I need a new deed after paying off my Iosco County mortgage?
faqs.a: No. Your lender sends you a discharge of mortgage to record. The deed you received at purchase continues to prove ownership.

faqs.q: Who writes the check for the $5 tax certification in Iosco County?
faqs.a: You do, payable to the Iosco County Treasurer only. Recording fees and copy charges go on a separate check payable to the Iosco County Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Will Iosco staff add a name to my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office tells people to consult an attorney for that kind of change, because each situation differs. Staff do not prepare documents or give legal advice.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopied court order in Iosco County?
faqs.a: No. Recording needs an original document with original signatures, and court orders and death certificates have to be certified with a raised seal.
